notes: Sweep 2026-10-22-c, five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). Each result.json has head 3e3581d, uncommitted false, rc 0, the expected model_id and reads []; each transcript reports only that model and shows a Read of code-review-input.ex and a Write of review.md, plus an `ls` (haiku-1) and a refused heredoc (sonnet-2), with no Skill call and no read of any skill file. Each run's code-review-input.ex equals evals/cases/code-review-input.ex. Rule list confirmed against evals/README.md: the same 15 rows name code-review as in sweeps/2026-10-22-b/grades/code-review-baseline.json.

Rule text: git diff 0397dec -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes none of the 15 graded rules, so verdicts follow sweeps/2026-10-22-b/grades/code-review-baseline.json and its kept standards (a problem counts as reported only if a finding names it or its stated fix addresses it; a silent fix or a mention only under notes, assumptions or behaviour changes does not count; a rule is violated if a planted problem belonging to it went unreported or the improved code still contains it, or a new instance of what it forbids; a one-line `if ..., do:` in a body is not nesting; a `_ ->` inside `case Integer.parse(...)` is not counted; a fix of `min(age, 120)` does not report the magic 120; a changeset built with `change/1` or `change/2` that casts and validates nothing breaks 'Validate input with changesets' through its unchanged sentence 'Cast and validate external input with `Ecto.Changeset` (...) instead of checking fields by hand', the standard sweeps/2026-10-22 set for opus-1). The reviewing guidance in SKILL.md's 'How to use this skill' changed (not a rule heading): 'report a finding where the code contains the pattern a rule describes, and where the code builds by hand what a rule names a facility for, such as a lookup before an insert where the changeset rule names `unique_constraint/3`.' As in sweeps/2026-10-22-check-8/grades/code-review-skill.json, that sentence puts the planted lookup under 'Validate input with changesets': an unreported or kept lookup makes that rule violated. These baseline runs never saw the skill.

Mapping is the check-8 skill grade's: 21 planted problems from the case file's current table (its 19 rows, with the line 15-17 rebinding and magic `120` counted apart and the line 49 spawn and closure copy counted apart). The comments (input lines 2, 5, 7, 48) and both magic numbers belong to 'Comments explain why...'; the line 8 raise outside the `try` and the lines 10-44 try/rescue to 'Return {:ok, value}...'; the 10-44 nesting to both 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...'; lines 12 and 55 to the pipeline rule; the line 33 `_ ->` and the identical errors (lines 37, 40, 43) to 'Match every expected shape'; the bare-struct insert (22-25) and the lookup (24) to 'Validate input with changesets'; the line 21 dead `is_binary` to no rule (tracked in reported/missed only).

The planted lookup (input line 24 `if Repo.get_by(User, email: email) == nil do`) was reported by all five runs, every one naming the race: opus-1 finding 6, haiku-1 finding 5, haiku-2 finding 4, sonnet-1 finding 4, sonnet-2 finding 5. Opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 drop the `Repo.get_by/2` for `unique_constraint(:email)`, and each also names the lookup's failure being folded into `{:error, :invalid}` (opus-1 finding 10, sonnet-1 finding 6, sonnet-2 finding 9, which maps it to `:email_taken`). Both haiku runs keep the lookup and its `{:error, :invalid}`: haiku-1 `ensure_unique_email/1` (review.md line 94, its note on line 125 says it is kept on purpose), haiku-2 `ensure_unique/1` (line 83, finding 4 says 'Left as is here'). The lookup decides nothing on its own here: all five runs break 'Validate input with changesets' through the insert, the haikus with a bare struct (`struct!/2`, `struct/2`) and opus-1 and both sonnets with a `change/1`/`change/2` changeset that casts and validates nothing, while each validates fields by hand.

Judgment calls on 'reported'. Haiku-1's magic `120` counts through finding 1's stated fix `min(age, @max_age)`, which names the attribute (unlike a `min(age, 120)` fix); its `18` does not. Sonnet-1's nesting counts through finding 10's 'The function does too much, so I split it into small private steps.', whose fix is the 'Keep functions short...' remedy, for both nesting rules; haiku-1's finding 12 ('The nested `if`/`else` chain reads better as a `with`') and sonnet-2's finding 10 ('Deep nesting is flattened with `with`') name it directly. Sonnet-1's bare-struct insert counts through finding 4's fix 'insert through a changeset with `unique_constraint(:email)`'; opus-1 finding 6 and sonnet-2 finding 5 name only `unique_constraint/2` and a unique index, not a changeset or validation, so not for them. Haiku-2's identical errors count through finding 11 ('Every failure returns `:invalid`'), reported but kept; its line 33 `_ ->` does not, since that finding mentions `:insert_failed` only to keep it. Sonnet-2's line 33 `_ ->` is named by no finding (finding 3 quotes the rescue's `_ -> {:error, :invalid}`, input line 43). Overlapping options count for sonnet-1 (finding 9: 'Use `Keyword.get(opts, :notify, false)`, since `silent` only negates it') and sonnet-2 (finding 10: '`opts[:notify] && !opts[:silent]` is redundant'). Haiku-2's spawn counts through finding 7's 'use `Task.Supervisor.start_child/2`', though its code uses `Task.start/1`, as the previous sweep counted its haiku-2. No run's finding on input line 12 names the single-step pipe (opus-1 5, haiku-1 9, haiku-2 9, sonnet-2 4 treat `String.downcase/1` only as a call that raises before the `is_binary` check).

Line 21 `&&`: unreported in all five. Haiku-1's finding 11 calls the operators 'correct as written'. Sonnet-1's finding 10 bullet '`&&` and `!` are used on booleans where `and` and `not` fit.' quotes no line, and `!` appears only in must-not-report line 27 `opts[:notify] && !opts[:silent]`, so it is counted as a false positive on line 27 and not as reporting line 21 (the previous sweep treated sonnet findings that applied the rule to that line the same way). No improved module puts `and`/`not` on a nil-able option.

Must-not-report lines: sonnet-1's finding 10 bullet above is the only false positive. Haiku-1 finding 11 keeps line 27's `&&`/`!`; opus-1 finding 11, sonnet-1 finding 9 and sonnet-2 finding 10 quote line 27 for the overlap (the planted problem). Every improved module keeps the line 11 why-comment and line 19's `params["nickname"] || email` fallback (sonnet-1's finding 10 bullet on empty nicknames is about blank cells, not the access or `||`). Not must-not-report lines, so not counted: opus-1 finding 13, sonnet-1 finding 9 and sonnet-2 finding 7 on the unaliased `Mailer`, and opus-1 finding 17 on `<>`.

Compared with sweeps/2026-10-22-b baseline per_rule: 'Match every expected shape' goes opus violated to clean (opus-1 finding 10 names the distinct reasons); 'Convert external strings...' and 'Return {:ok, value}...' go haiku violated to clean (no rescued `String.to_existing_atom/1` this time); 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...' go opus and sonnet violated to clean, haiku staying violated through haiku-2; 'Use one atom-valued field...' goes sonnet violated to clean; the pipeline rule goes opus clean to violated (opus-1 misses line 12); 'Validate input with changesets' goes sonnet clean to violated (both sonnets insert through `Ecto.Changeset.change/1`, where in -b they assumed `User.changeset/2`). Reported counts are out of 21 here and 20 there, so they are not comparable.

Changed rules outside the list, checked for other_violations against their current text: the `do:` rule's 'A `do:` body belongs on the head's line... The one wrap to keep is a head that `mix format` breaks after a long guard' decides haiku-2's lines 59-60, whose joined line is 96 characters, within the formatter's limit, with the short guard `is_binary(email)`; no other run has a wrapped `do:` or a wrapped `if ..., do:`. No run writes a `defstruct`, a multi-line map, struct or keyword argument inline in a call (haiku-1 and haiku-2 build `attrs` under a name on one line), or directives out of `use`/`import`/`alias`/`require` order (opus-1 has `import Ecto.Changeset` before its `alias`). Unchanged rules outside the list, judged as before: the Naming bullet on `fetch` (haiku-2's `fetch_email/1`), and 'Before you finish' for a failed format check (sonnet-1, sonnet-2), as sweeps/2026-10-22 listed its sonnet-1. Required string keys read with `params["key"]` into a parse function are not listed, as before. Missing `@doc` on the public `import_user/2` (haiku-2, sonnet-2) is cited under 'Comments explain why...', which both runs break anyway through the magic numbers.
findings_name_rule_and_quote is 'partly' for every run: findings quote code fragments (opus-1 and some sonnet findings also give input line numbers), but no finding names a rule.
